title: gh api -F content=@<(process substitution) fails silently-ish on Windows Git Bash — write to a real temp file instead
fix: On Windows Git Bash, `gh api -F field=@<(...)` (process substitution) does not work — gh tries to open the `/proc/<pid>/fd/NN` path directly and Windows can't resolve it, even though the same `<(...)` works fine for other commands. Always write process-substitution-style intermediate content (e.g. base64-encoded file bodies for Contents API PUTs) to a real temp file on disk first, then reference it with `-F field=@realfile`. This is on top of the already-known `-F` vs `-f` distinction (capital `-F` for `@file` reads) and the base64-encoding-required-for-blobs rule — this is a third, independent gotcha about `<(...)` specifically, not just about `-f` vs `-F` or encoding.
confirmed_via: On this Windows machine's Git Bash (Bash tool), `gh api --method PUT repos/OWNER/REPO/contents/PATH -F content=@<(base64 -w0 file.md)` returned `error parsing "content" value: open /proc/<pid>/fd/63: The system cannot find the path specified.` for all four files attempted in one loop (ai-news-channel PR #22). Rewriting the same loop to `base64 -w0 file.md > file.md.b64` then `-F content=@file.md.b64` succeeded on the first try for all four, verified via each PUT response's `commit.sha` plus a follow-up Contents API GET diffed against the intended text.
source_run: begb0037admin/cat, ai-news-channel PR #22 (EP06/EP07 Approval status + EP06-EP08 QA report episode-number fixes), 7 August 2026

title: gh pr create fails with "you must first push the current branch" right after a successful git push -u — pass --repo/--base/--head explicitly
fix: If `gh pr create` claims a branch isn't pushed right after a push that visibly succeeded, don't retry the push — add explicit `--repo OWNER/REPO --base main --head <branch>` flags to `gh pr create` instead. `gh`'s local tracking-ref detection can be unreliable on this machine even when the remote branch and commits are genuinely present.
confirmed_via: On this Windows machine (Git Bash), after `git push -u origin cat/ep06-ep07-master-source-notebooklm-chunks` succeeded (branch visibly created on GitHub, `git branch -vv` output notwithstanding showed no tracking ref recorded locally), a plain `gh pr create --title ... --body ...` immediately failed with `aborted: you must first push the current branch to a remote, or use the --head flag`. Re-running with `gh pr create --repo begb0037admin/ai-news-channel --base main --head cat/ep06-ep07-master-source-notebooklm-chunks --title ... --body ...` succeeded on the first try (ai-news-channel PR #25).
source_run: Cat, ai-news-channel PR #25 (EP06/EP07 Master Source, Chat Chunks, Audio Overview Prompt)

title: episode-artwork font path must be OS-detected, never trusted from shared config
fix: 03_Spotify_Podcast/tools/episode-artwork/episode_template_config.json is read AND written by both the Windows (.bat) and Mac (.command) launchers, so any OS-specific absolute path saved into it (e.g. "font") will break the other OS next time it runs. The fix pattern: never hardcode an OS path in a config file shared by both platforms — instead have the script itself branch on platform.system() ("Darwin" vs "Windows") and only trust a config-supplied override if Path(...).is_file() is true on the current machine. Applies to any other cross-platform path fields this tool (or similar shared-config tools in this repo) might grow later — e.g. font, but the same logic would apply to any hardcoded filesystem path.
confirmed_via: PR #26 on begb0037admin/ai-news-channel — ran the fixed render_episode_template.py directly on this Windows machine three ways: (1) config "font" blank -> resolved to C:\WINDOWS\Fonts\impact.ttf, exit 0; (2) config "font" forced to the stale Mac path /System/Library/Fonts/Supplemental/Impact.ttf that doesn't exist on Windows (the exact original bug) -> no longer crashes, correctly falls through to the Windows path; (3) config "font" forced to a valid existing Windows path -> respected. All three exit 0, verified via layer-manifest.json and printed Font: line. Mac (Darwin) branch not tested live (no Mac available) — verified by code review only, byte-identical to the prior unconditional default path.
source_run: Cat task 2026-08-07 — fix episode-artwork Impact font path bug (PR #26)
